📄 Analyse a paper

Give Appuscholer a research paper and learn to read it. Ask your own questions, or let it walk you through the paper stage by stage: the gap, the design, the sample, the statistics, the limits. Each answer comes with quotations from the paper, and the app checks that every quotation really is in the paper.

Short talks on reading papers, statistics, scales, study design, writing and ethics. No paper needed.

🔍 Closeness check

Compares the document you are writing with texts you already hold: papers on your Reading shelf, your other documents, and any passage you paste in. It marks every run of words that matches a source word for word, and says where. Everything happens in this browser. Nothing is sent anywhere, and no AI is used.

What it cannot do. It sees only the sources you tick or paste. It does not search the web, books or journals you have not loaded, and it cannot see an idea copied in new words. Use it to catch a paraphrase that hugs a paper you read. It is not a plagiarism verdict, and it is not a similarity report for your institution.

📖 Words and grammar

Look up a word and keep the ones you want to learn, then check your writing for common slips. Nothing changes in your document unless you press Apply.

Grammar check

Checks the text you have selected, or the whole document if nothing is selected. The rules are free and instant. The AI check sends the text to your AI provider and reads the first 9,000 characters.

✍ My Writing Style

Teach Appuscholar to write like YOU. Upload your files — Word, PDF or text.

Only your own writing

Use text you wrote yourself, without AI and without copying. A published paper by someone else will teach the app their voice, not yours, and passing it off as your style is misuse. Your declaration is saved here and appears in your AI-use statement.

Check that the samples are yours: a short typed paraphrase

Read the passage, then write it again in your own words in the box. Pasting is switched off. The app compares your typing with your samples on four habits. It is a rough check, and it cannot prove who wrote anything.

Vocabulary check: ten words

Choose the meaning of each word, or "I do not know". Ten words give only a rough level. The level keeps suggestions to words you are likely to know. Technical terms of your field stay.

Does it sound like me?

The app writes the practice passage in your learned voice. Judge it.

🔬 Research

Search OpenAlex and PubMed live, free, no install — pick what's relevant, then draft a literature review or find a research gap, grounded only in the abstracts you found.

🎯 Narrow my topic

A topic that is too broad gives thousands of papers and no clear gap. Check how crowded yours is, pick a sub-topic, or let the helper ask you the questions a supervisor would.

Filter these results
Filters only hide papers from view; nothing is deleted. The last two use the Quick read, so a paper you have not quick-read yet is hidden while either is set, and a field the Quick read could not confirm counts as unknown. PubMed results carry no open-access flag, so the open-access filter hides them. Citation count and sample size do not measure the quality of a study.

Drafted strictly from the papers you checked above — always verify the actual sources before citing them.

Whose writing is this?

A paper by someone else is kept as a source. It is not counted as your writing, not used to learn your style and not shown in "% yours". You can change this later with the 📄 button.

📊 My writing

Where the words in your documents came from. It counts text typed in this editor against text inserted from an AI suggestion or the chat. It cannot see your thinking, and text you retype from an AI answer counts as yours. No targets, no score. It is just a mirror.

👋 Welcome back

Answer in your own words. Nobody grades these, and the app does not read them. They are saved on this computer so you can see how your thinking moved.

🎓 Viva question

The AI asks one question an examiner might ask about the passage you selected (or the end of your document). Answer from your own head. There is no AI help in the answer box, because the point is to rehearse the real moment.

This is the language the AI writes in — your paper, explanations, stats write-ups — separate from the interface language toggle above. Saved with the open project, or as your default when no project is open.

Paper search uses OpenAlex. Without a key it has a small free daily allowance, and a heavy day can use it up. A free key from openalex.org (Settings, API) gives ten times more. The key stays on this computer and is left out of backups.

The AI uses this to pitch explanations and examples at your field. Psychology has the most tools built in; the others are being added.

Appuscholar privately saves a copy of your own writing from each document on this computer — whatever you typed yourself, skipping anything an AI suggestion inserted. Nothing is uploaded anywhere. The idea is a future tool that learns to write in your own voice from this. Turn off any time; your documents themselves are never affected either way.

The text of that one request then goes to the other provider you saved a key for, and a message tells you which one answered. Switch this off if you want every request to stay with one provider.

Back up your work

Your documents, citations and projects live only in this browser. Clearing the browser data erases them. Download a backup file now and then, and keep it somewhere safe. It never contains your AI key or access code.

If you lose this phone or computer

⚠ Because this app runs as a local file, every HTML file on your computer shares one storage area. A key saved with Remember on this computer can be read by any other HTML file you open. The passphrase option encrypts it so those files see only scrambled text.

📚 Reading shelf

Add PDFs you have the right to read. Appuscholar reads each one in your browser and keeps only the extracted text, on this computer. The PDF file itself is not stored and nothing is uploaded. Scanned PDFs without a text layer cannot be read.

📋 Scale library

Published scales with the owner's own wording. The text is fixed and never rewritten by the AI, because a reworded item is no longer the validated item. Each scale shows its licence record. Check that the terms fit your use before you put a scale in a study.

❓ Help & Troubleshooting

  
Most problems have a quick fix below. Check here first — it's faster than waiting on an email.


  

  

    
    
  


  

    🔑 My access code won't work
    
Paste the whole code, including the dot in the middle, with no extra spaces or line breaks — copying from some apps adds a stray character at the start or end. Codes also expire; if the date has passed, you'll need a fresh one from whoever gave you Appuscholar.

  

  

    🔌 My AI key stopped working, or I lost it
    
Open ⚙ AI Provider / Key at the top right, pick your provider again, and follow the link to generate a new one — it's free and takes under a minute. Your key lives only in this browser; nothing to recover from a server.

  

  

    💾 My work disappeared after closing the tab or clearing my browser
    
Everything is saved only in this browser, on this computer — never on a server. Clearing site data, switching browsers, or moving to a new computer wipes it with no way back. Use ⬇ Download in the document toolbar regularly to keep a copy outside the browser.

  

  

    🖥 The page looks broken, or won't load properly
    
Try a hard refresh — Ctrl+Shift+R on Windows, Cmd+Shift+R on a Mac — or open it in Chrome or Edge if you're on something else. Both render this app best.

  

  

    हि Something stayed in English after switching to Hindi
    
A few things stay in English on purpose — statistical test names, citation style names (APA, MLA), and the external AI-provider sign-up pages — since those are the exact terms you'll meet everywhere else too. Anything other than that is a genuine bug worth reporting below.

  


  

    
Still stuck? Tell us what happened and we'll help directly.

🎯 Sample size and power

  
How many people does the study need, how much power does a given sample have, or what is the smallest effect a given sample can detect. Everything is computed here from the exact noncentral distributions; nothing is uploaded.

  

    

      

    

      

  

  

    

    

    

    

  

  

    

    

    

    

    

  

  

  

  

  
🎓 Learn: watch power happen (SIMULATED)
    
Run a few hundred pretend studies of the same size on a computer and see how many of them find a real effect. Everything here is SIMULATED. No real people, no data file, and nothing here can be copied into a study. It exists to show why a small study misses real effects and why the studies that do find it overstate it.

    
Two groups of equal size. The true difference between them is the effect size d you choose. Each pretend study draws new people and runs an independent-samples t-test at alpha .05, two-tailed.

📝 CTRI registration readiness
